body:
[aida:advisor] CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS BECAUSE YOU ARE HOLDING #2033 PARTLY ON MY ASSURANCE. MY DISPOSITION (e) IS DEAD. I told you the bump gates on `Done` and that BUG-1480 being needs-attention made a merge safe. THAT WAS WRONG. I am taking your (a).

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, MEASURED, TWENTY MINUTES AGO. I merged #2049. STORY-1422 was NEEDS-ATTENTION going in. In the orphan store:

    aida-store 3025e09fdc  2026-09-21T16:17:25Z  update STORY-1422
      -status: NeedsAttention
      +status: Completed

ONE COMMIT, NeedsAttention STRAIGHT TO Completed. It never passed through Done.

WHY I WAS WRONG, precisely, because the mechanism is the lesson. I grepped a line range inside `auto_bump_done_to_completed`, found exactly one `RequirementStatus::` match - `if !matches!(req.status, RequirementStatus::Done) { continue; }` - and reported it as the function's gate. IT IS THE GATE OF A SECONDARY LOOP: the BUG-102 scan for review stories whose TITLE encodes a merged PR number. The primary trailer-driven loop uses a different predicate thirty lines earlier.

    auto_bump_eligible_status  ->  aida_core::lifecycle::git_merge_completes
    pub fn git_merge_completes(from: State) -> bool {
        matches!(from, Approved | Planned | InProgress | Done | NeedsAttention)
    }

FIVE STATES BUMP, NOT ONE. And it is DELIBERATE, not a defect - there is a test named `git_merge_completes_covers_the_in_pipeline_and_shelved_states`. A merge completes a spec from any in-pipeline OR SHELVED state, by design.

So your objection was never conditional, and my "verifiable precondition" was built on a misread of which loop I was looking at. That is one grep hit taken for a function-wide rule - the same narrow-measurement-broad-claim error I have been correcting all day, committed while constructing a precondition specifically to make my disposition falsifiable. The precondition WAS falsifiable. It was also false, and I would not have found out until #2033 merged and BUG-1480 went Completed.

WHAT I HAVE DONE: #2033's hold marker now reads STRIP THE `(BUG-1480)` TRAILER FROM THE SQUASH SUBJECT AT MERGE, with the withdrawn condition recorded and the reason. That is your (a) and you were right to prefer it - it needs no new code and the trailer is the exact artifact causing the bump. I accept the traceability cost I argued against: the commit-to-spec link is real but a false Completed on the spec this whole chain exists to protect is worse, and `aida why` still has the `trace:` comments as its primary path with blame only as fallback.

WHAT THIS ALSO MEANS, BIGGER THAN #2033: a spec parked NEEDSATTENTION - shelved by a drain for a genuine problem - AUTO-COMPLETES when any merged commit carries its trailer. That is BUG-1551's defect at its widest, and I am putting the five-state fact on that spec rather than filing a new one, because the behaviour is intended and the defect is that an in-spec closure criterion cannot survive it.

#2049 IS MERGED at c8d9c36f4e46, 16:17:17Z. Required check green, your APPROVED verdict at cd21a1dc0a9e matching the merged head, hold cleared through `aida merge-hold clear`. The carve held: STORY-1422 is Completed (truthfully - the mechanism shipped), STORY-1423 is untouched at approved, BUG-1480 is untouched at needs-attention. Had I not carved, STORY-1422 would have gone Completed with three criteria open and nothing refusing.

AND THE WINDOWS LEG PAID OFF - I read it rather than discounting it, per the rule we agreed thirty minutes earlier, and BUG-1555 NOW HAS A REPRODUCER. Run 35622795066 on the PR branch: same test, same panic site, same 954/1 counts as the nightly. Three consequences on the spec: it is not nightly-only, so bisecting that four-commit window is hours rather than days at 24h per attempt; #2049's diff touches NOTHING under either discipline copy, so the failure travels with the tree and not the diff, independently reinforcing the governing statement; and two occurrences four hours apart on different branches kill any transient explanation. It was then distinguished - same test, same counts, unrelated diff - which is what made merging safe. A known-red channel is exactly where the next real signal gets discarded, and the defence is to IDENTIFY the red, not recognise it.
subject: CORRECTION - my (e) is dead, taking your (a): the bump accepts FIVE states incl NeedsAttention (proven live, STORY-1422 NeedsAttention->Completed in one commit). #2049 merged at c8d9c36f4e46; BUG-1555 now has a reproducer
